A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, references, and complete Appendices A–D. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Figures 1 and 2 report original simulations of gradient descent, measuring recovery against sample ratio, dimension, and iteration count.

after.justification: Figures 1 and 2 retain these original simulation results, including recovery curves and sample- and iteration-complexity fits.

M1.justification: The spherical correlation-loss dynamics, quadratic and truncated activations, and Euclidean squared-loss GD from small initialization remain unchanged. The sign convention added in v2 does not alter the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian single-index problems with quadratic and truncated quadratic activations, using the same dimension and sample-ratio coverage.

E2.justification: The same GD configurations participate in Figures 1–2. Neither version reports an empirical one-pass SGD baseline, and the additional related-work citations are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The plotted experiments retain their learning rates, iteration budget, truncation threshold, initialization scale, and sample ratios. The revised theoretical definition of strong recovery does not change the plotted squared-overlap and norm metrics.

E4.justification: The truncation comparison and checks of logarithmic sample and iteration scaling remain unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: V1 states that Figure 1 averages 128 random seeds and Figure 2 averages 1024. V2 removes both disclosures without restoring them elsewhere. This reduces repeated-run reporting; it does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: All six plot panels in Figures 1–2 are identical across versions, including curves, shaded bands, and fitted relationships. No empirical result entries or reported performance trends change.

T1.justification: Equation (2.1) changes strong recovery from convergence to θ⋆ to convergence to either θ⋆ or −θ⋆. Section 4 correspondingly introduces sign-minimized error and an explicit sign convention. The sample-complexity bounds, convergence rates, and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The main sample-complexity separation and logarithmic iteration claims remain, but exact recovery is now explicitly qualified as recovery up to sign. Sections 1.1 and 5 also omit the random-initialization qualifier from their novelty statements, although Theorem 4.1 retains that assumption.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses sign ambiguity and emphasizes why even targets require analysis beyond finitely many data passes. It also adds the qualification that earlier overparameterized landscape results do not isolate whether the benefit comes from data reuse or overparameterization.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures concerning learning rates, truncation thresholds, initialization, and iteration budgets remain unchanged. No hardware or code/data-access information changes; the removed repeated-run disclosures are assessed under E5.

R1.justification: V2 adds Oko et al. (2024) and two Diakonikolas et al. (2025) references, and expands positioning against two-pass loss modification and overparameterized phase retrieval. The Xie et al. attribution removed from the main proof sketch remains in Appendix D.5.2.

P1.justification: The abstract, opening motivation, and related-work discussion receive localized rewrites and expansions, alongside small wording and bibliographic corrections. The section sequence and overall proof organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 6 to page 7, captions are shortened, and equations and surrounding text reflow. V2 also colors citations and cross-references. The plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The sign-aware recovery definition and Section 4 convention correct the stated target for an even activation, while the expanded prior-work discussion improves precision. These limited gains outweigh the loss of transparency from deleting the 128- and 1024-seed averaging disclosures. The revision adds no new empirical evidence or appendix proof development.
